topics.title: Hub
topics.content: hub is layer 1 device that connects one or two computers. A hub is usually termed as a ‘dumb’ device because when a hub receives data, it simply sends data to every other connected device, regardless of the intended recipient; in other word it broadcasts the data across all the connected devices.

topics.title: Switch
topics.content: switch is a layer 2 device that connects one or two computers. A switch send the data to the intended device based on mac address (it unicast the data)

topics.title: Router
topics.content:
Router is a layer 3 device that connects different networks. A router can calculate the best route for sending data from one point to another using an IP address.
 

Routing protocols: Routing protocols are sets of rules and procedures that routers use to communicate with each other to find and select the best paths for forwarding data packets across networks.

Routing Protocols & Easy Two-Sentence Descriptions
RIP (Routing Information Protocol)
RIP uses hop count to find the best path — like choosing roads based only on “fewest turns.”
It’s simple but old, and routers using RIP don’t know how fast or congested a link is.

OSPF (Open Shortest Path First)
OSPF builds a full map of the network using link-state information — like having Google Maps with traffic data.
It picks the best path based on cost (speed, bandwidth), making it fast and intelligent.

EIGRP (Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol)
EIGRP is Cisco’s smart hybrid protocol that picks routes using several metrics (delay, bandwidth, reliability).
It converges quickly, like a GPS that instantly recalculates if a road closes.

BGP (Border Gateway Protocol)
BGP runs the internet by letting ISPs exchange routes — like countries negotiating which roads connect their borders.
It chooses paths based on policies, not speed, making it extremely powerful but complex.

IS-IS (Intermediate System to Intermediate System)
IS-IS works similar to OSPF, using link-state logic, but is more scalable in very large networks.
Big telecom networks use it because it handles huge topologies with ease.

Static Routing (manual routes)
Static routes are manually added by the admin — like telling a router “always use this exact road.”
They’re simple and predictable but don’t adapt automatically if a link fails.

topics.title: MAC address
topics.content: A MAC (Media Access Control address) address is a unique, permanent identifier assigned to a network interface card (NIC) by its manufacturer, used to identify a device on a local network.

topics.title: IP address
topics.content:
IP address: (internet protocol address): its a unique number assigned to every device connected to the internet.
In the world of the internet everything will be remembered or identified by the ip address.
There are two types of IP addresses.
Private IP: which are non-routable in nature. (LAN)
Public IP: which are routable from the internet. (WAN)

ISP: internet service provider

The IP that can not be tracked from the internet is known as non routable or private IP

The IP that can be tracked from the internet is known as routable or public IP
 

Private IP address Range

topics.title: Difference between Private IP and Public IP
topics.content:
Public IP Address
A public IP is your home’s main address on the Internet, used by the outside world to reach your network.
It is unique globally, assigned by your ISP, and can be accessed over the internet.
👉 Real-world example:
Like your house address — anyone can send you a letter.


 

Private IP Address
A private IP is the internal address inside your local network, used for devices to communicate with your router.
It is not reachable from the internet directly and must go through NAT to reach outside.

👉 Real-world example:
Like room numbers inside your house — only useful inside, not visible to the outside world.

topics.title: Address Translators
topics.content:
it is the process of converting one IP address to another. Usually translation happens from private to public IP address.

NAT & PAT
NAT: Network address translation. it is a Private IP address or local address that is translated into the public IP address.
PAT: Port Address translation. Private IP addresses are translated into the public IP address through port numbers.

topics.title: Ports list
Threeway hand shake
topics.content:
• It is a method used in the TCP/IP network to create the connection between two hosts.
  • It's a three step process that requires both client and server to exchange the SYN and ACK packages before actual data communication begins.

  •  

Process of three way hand shake

  • The process starts from the client sending the SYN packet to the server which it wants to communicate with, the objective of the packet is to check if the server is open for new connection.
  • If the server is open for the new connection the server will respond with SYN/ACK pocket.
  • Then the client responds with the acknowledgement ACK which establishes the connections between client and server.
  • Upon completion of this process the actual data communication starts between the client and server.

topics.title: Four way hand shake
topics.content:
Four way hand shake is for terminating the connection.

 

1. Host A → Host B: FIN flag set.

2. Host B → Host A: ACK flag set.

3. Host B → Host A: FIN flag set.

4. Host A → Host B: ACK flag set.

topics.title: Types of connections
topics.content: In the computer network majorly there are two types of communication established process which are TCP and UDP

topics.title: TCP
topics.content:
Transmission Control Protocol
TCP is a layer 4 communication protocol within the internet protocol which ensures reliable, ordered, and error- checked delivery of data between devices. When two devices establish a TCP connection, they perform a three-way handshake to confirm each other’s presence and agree on parameters for data exchange.
Use cases: web browsing, file transfer, email, online banking and remote access.

topics.title: UDP
topics.content:
User datagram protocol
a layer 4 communication protocol used in the internet’s network layer, transport layer, and session layer. Unlike TCP it sends data as independent packets called datagrams without first establishing a dedicated connection. This means UDP does not guarantee delivery, order, or error correction, it simply sends data and hopes it get delivered.
Use cases: VoIP Calls, video streaming, gaming,

topics.title: Difference between TCP and UDP
TCP/IP packet structure
topics.content:
In a computer network the data transfer happens in the form of packets. Packet mainly consist of three layers (IP header, TCP header, payload)

 

IP Headers: The IP header contains information needed to route the packet across networks, such as source and destination IP addresses. It ensures the packet is delivered to the correct device, even across multiple routers.


TCP Headers: The TCP header carries connection-related details like source Port , Destination Port, sequence numbers, acknowledgment numbers, and flags. It enables reliable, ordered, and error-checked communication between two devices.

 

Payload: The payload is the actual data being transported — such as HTTP content, API responses, or file data. It sits after the headers and is delivered to the application at the receiving end

topics.title: Flags
topics.content:
Flags are control bits that manage TCP communication and help to identify the status of communication or connection status.


 

Most common in interview questions: SYN, ACK, FIN, RST.

topics.title: Difference between PSH and URG flag.
topics.content:
PSH: “Deliver this data to the application immediately.”

 

URG: “Some data in this packet is urgent — process it first.”

topics.title: Ports and Protocols
topics.content:
In computer network communication takes place between the client and server by using dedicated ports and protocols which helps to have smoother communication between client and server.
 

What Are Protocols?
Protocols are rules and standards that define how data is sent, received, and processed across a network.


What Are Ports?
Ports are virtual communication endpoints used by computers to identify specific services or applications during network communication. In total there are 65,535 ports

topics.title: What is DHCP
topics.content:
DHCP stands for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.

Port number 67 - DHCP server and 68 client DHCP

 

DHCP is a server that automatically assigns the private IP address and important network configuration details to devices when they join the network.
DHCP follows a 4-step sequence called DORA:
 

Instead of manually configuring each device, DHCP does it automatically.

 

Apart from assigning the IP address the DHCP server will also assign some of the other information as well. And they are subnet mask, default gateway, DNS server and lease period(renewal duration)

topics.title: what is DORA
topics.content:
1. Discover: when a computer is configured to get the IP address automatically, then the computer broadcasts a Discover message to the DHCP server.
  2. Offer: Once the ‘discover’ message hits the DHCP server, the DHCP server offers the available IP address within the subnet(group of IP address).
  3. Request: Then the client will respond with the request message to DHCP server through unicast
    Acknowledge: Then the DHCP server acknowledges the request by assigning the IP address to the client.

 

 

Initial default IP of DHCP client is 0.0.0.0

Default ip of DHCP  server 255.255.255.255

After the DORA process an private IP address is assigned

topics.title: Why is DHCP Important?
topics.content:
• Eliminates manual IP configuration
  • Prevents IP conflicts
  • Saves time in large networks
  • Allows centralized management
  • Supports both IPv4 and IPv6

topics.title: Where DHCP Is Used?
topics.content:
• Home Wi-Fi networks
  • Corporate networks
  • Cloud and virtual environments
  • Internet providers (ISP networks)

topics.title: What does DHCP do?
topics.content:
When a device connects to a network (like your phone connecting to Wi-Fi), DHCP automatically provides:

  1. IP Address A unique address for the device on the network.
  2. Subnet Mask Defines the network portion and host portion of the IP.
  3. Default Gateway Router address for communication outside the network.
  4. DNS Server Addresses Used to translate domain names (like google.com) to IPs.
  5. Lease Time How long the device can use the assigned IP.

topics.title: What happens if no DHCP server is not available on the network?
topics.content: The client gets an IP from APIPA that is automatically private IP address in range the range is between 169.254.0.0 to  169 254.255.255

topics.title: What happens when a DHCP server once out of IP addresses?
topics.content: when DHCP server runs out of addresses your Subnet is said to be over subscribed then DHCP server refuses to assign an IP address and until a device in the network release an IP or makes it available again or after the lease time expires

topics.title: What is APIPA?
topics.content:
APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing)
Range: 169.254.0.0 – 169.254.255.255

topics.title: When does APIPA happen?
topics.content:
• When a DHCP client cannot reach any DHCP server
  • After multiple retries fail
  • Windows, macOS, and Linux may assign APIPA automatically

topics.title: What does APIPA do?
topics.content:
• Gives the client a self-assigned IP so it can communicate only locally (ex: 169.254.34.56 )
  • No internet or router access
  • Limited to local subnet communication

topics.title: How to close open ports in cybersecurity?
topics.content:
1. Identify the open ports

    Use tools like nmap or netstat.

    Determine unused ports.

Review the list and identify ports not in use.

  1. Block or close ports

Firewall: configure your firewall to block incoming traffic on unused ports.

  1. Disable services: stop services listening on unused ports.

Common methods: 
Windows: use windows defender firewall.
Linux: use UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall), or iptables

topics.title: OSI model
topics.content:
OSI (Open system interconnection)model

 

  • It's a reference model that helps to understand how the data flows between client and server in a computer network.
  • The OSI model contains 7 layers and each layer contributes to specific activity to transfer the data from one network to another.

 

  • In OSI layers like application, presentation and session acts as software
  • Layers like network, data link, and physical works as a hardware component

The transport layer works as the heart ❤️ of the OSI model to connect and transfer data between one network to another. 

 

Application layer:  the interface between user and the computer. 
    Protocols: http, smtp, https.

 

Presentation layer: 

  • The presentation layer is also called the Translation layer.
  • The data from the application layer is extracted here and translated as required format to transmit over the network.
  • The data encryption, decryption, encoding and decoding takes place in the presentation layer.
    Protocols: TLS/SSL (Transport Layer Security / Secure Sockets Layer).JPEG, MPEG, GIF,

 

Session layer: 

  • It is responsible for establishment of connection, maintenance of sessions, authentication and security.

    Protocols used in the Session Layer are NetBIOS, PPTP.

     

Transport layer:

  • In the transport layer the data will be in segments.

  • It is responsible for ensuring the data is transmitted in the same order and no duplication of the data and it also ensures the error control and flow control of the data


    protocols used here are: TCP, UDP

 

Network layer: 

  • Here the data will be in the form of packets.
  • The network layer works for the transmission of data from one host to the other located in different networks.
  • This has devices like routers and firewalls.

    Protocols : IP, ARP

 

Data Link layer:

  • The data will be in the form of frames.
  • The data link layer is responsible for the node-to-node delivery of the message.

  • The main function of this layer is to make sure data transfer is error-free from one node to another, over the physical layer.

    Protocols: wi-fi, ethernet

     

Physical Layer:
It is responsible for the actual physical connection between the devices. 
The physical layer contains information in the form of bits. (Raw data)
Protocols: hub, bluetooth.
